units.rhetorical_move: states the task as a bare infinitive chain
units.function: list the jobs without a subject

original_instantiations: three jobs are listed with no subject
the list runs study, build, offer

units.source_excerpt: To study the issues, build a pricing system and offer recommendations.
units.reusable_pattern: Open by listing the jobs as bare infinitives.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a subject the sentence lacks.

units.rhetorical_move: builds one model and extends it
units.function: name the base theory and the extension

original_instantiations: the primary model rests on one theory
a second theory extends it

units.source_excerpt: We build our primary model on one theory and extend it by referring to another.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the base theory and the theory that extends it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not swap which theory is the base.

units.rhetorical_move: says both sides make every efforts

original_instantiations: both parties maximize their own benefits
efforts is written in the plural

units.source_excerpt: They both make every efforts to maximize their own benefits.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep every efforts as the writer's phrasing.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not correct efforts to effort when quoting.

units.rhetorical_move: casts government as a social planner
units.function: give the third player a role

original_instantiations: the government is called a social planner
its aim is to maximize social utility

units.source_excerpt: The government, as a social planner, maximizes social utility.
units.reusable_pattern: Introduce a third party with as plus a role.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not give the planner a different aim.

units.rhetorical_move: divides a risk into categories
units.function: split one risk before weighting it

original_instantiations: one risk splits into three categories
each category depends on different traits

units.source_excerpt: We divide the risk into three primary and possible categories.
units.reusable_pattern: Divide a risk into numbered categories before weighting them.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not weight the risk whole.

units.rhetorical_move: uses a method because data are scarce
units.function: justify a method by missing data

original_instantiations: a weighting method is chosen
the reason is that few data exist in the field

units.source_excerpt: We employ a weighting method given that few data are available.
units.reusable_pattern: Justify a method with given that plus the missing data.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the data exist.

units.rhetorical_move: warns the utility is miscalculated
units.function: name the omission and its failure

original_instantiations: ignoring the network effect miscalculates social utility
the miscalculation makes the pricing system fail

units.source_excerpt: Social utility is greatly miscalculated if the network effect is ignored.
units.reusable_pattern: Warn that one omission miscalculates the result and breaks the system.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat the omission as harmless.

units.rhetorical_move: offers a named tax as the remedy
units.function: name the instrument that erases the harm

original_instantiations: a named tax or subsidy is the remedy
it erases the externality and raises social utility

units.source_excerpt: With a named tax or subsidy, governments can erase the externality.
units.reusable_pattern: Offer a named instrument with with, then state what it erases.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not rename the instrument.

units.rhetorical_move: uses a four-line memo header
units.function: head the letter with to, from, subject, date

original_instantiations: the header names the recipient by office
subject and date follow on their own lines

units.source_excerpt: The memo header gives recipient, sender, subject and date on separate lines.
units.reusable_pattern: Head a policy memo with four labeled lines.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the date.

units.rhetorical_move: says the memo provides an overview

original_instantiations: the memo offers an overview
the overview covers models, results and recommendations

units.source_excerpt: This memo provides an overview of the models, the results and the recommendations.
units.reusable_pattern: Open a memo by stating what overview it provides.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not promise content the memo lacks.

units.rhetorical_move: says the team build two models

original_instantiations: parameters are introduced and two models follow
build stays in the present

units.source_excerpt: We introduced parameters and build two prime models.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep the tense shift from introduced to build.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not smooth the tense when quoting.

units.rhetorical_move: says information is exposed automatically
units.function: describe the harm of easy collection

original_instantiations: preferences are exposed after online shopping
phone numbers leak for advertising

units.source_excerpt: Tons of information on preferences are automatically exposed after shopping online.
units.reusable_pattern: Describe data exposure as automatic, then name the harm.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not soften automatically.

units.rhetorical_move: gives the other side of privacy
units.function: balance the harm with a benefit

original_instantiations: private data also brings benefits
customization and epidemic control are the examples

units.source_excerpt: Private information brings benefits only if it is known to others in some cases.
units.reusable_pattern: Balance a harm by stating the condition under which it becomes a benefit.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the condition.

units.rhetorical_move: refuses to rush to a conclusion

original_instantiations: rushing to one conclusion is called inappropriate
the conclusion is that privacy stays with the individual

units.source_excerpt: It is inappropriate to rush to the conclusion that privacy must stay private.
units.reusable_pattern: Refuse a verdict with it is inappropriate to rush.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not rush to the verdict anyway.

units.rhetorical_move: reduces society to three components

original_instantiations: society has three components
they are individuals, organizations and governments

units.source_excerpt: We assume society has three components: individuals, organizations and governments.
units.reusable_pattern: State an assumption as a count of named players.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a fourth player.

units.rhetorical_move: makes one variable the sole determinant

original_instantiations: one variable is the sole determinant
the others are set aside to simplify

units.source_excerpt: We decide that one variable is the sole determinant in the base model.
units.reusable_pattern: Simplify by naming the sole determinant.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not bring the dropped causes back silently.

units.rhetorical_move: says more information is naturally more valuable

original_instantiations: benefit rises with the amount of information
the rise is called natural

units.source_excerpt: Naturally, the benefit increases with a larger amount of information.
units.reusable_pattern: Mark an assumption as natural when it is not derived.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present naturally as a proof.

units.rhetorical_move: sets a two-stage sequential game

original_instantiations: the game has two stages and perfect information
it predicts both parties' behavior

units.source_excerpt: We set a dynamic perfect-information two-stage sequential game.
units.reusable_pattern: Name a game by its information and its stages.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not change the number of stages.

units.rhetorical_move: predicts every outcome by parameters

original_instantiations: every market outcome is predicted
each outcome belongs to one parameter setting

units.source_excerpt: By discussing the equilibrium, we predict every market outcome under different settings.
units.reusable_pattern: Say the equilibrium predicts every outcome, one per setting.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim an outcome outside the settings.

units.rhetorical_move: lets government offer a recommended price

original_instantiations: the government offers a recommended price
surveillance makes the market more effective

units.source_excerpt: Governments use an elaborate pricing system to offer a recommended price.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the planner an elaborate system and say what it offers.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call the price mandatory.

units.rhetorical_move: picks the second of two methods

original_instantiations: two meanings of the right are defined
the second is called more appropriate

units.source_excerpt: We find it more appropriate for government to adopt the second method.
units.reusable_pattern: Define two options and call one more appropriate.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not skip the rejected option.

units.rhetorical_move: says privacy can also be traded
units.function: hold both a right and a market

original_instantiations: privacy is a human right
it can still be traded at the owner's will

units.source_excerpt: Privacy should be a human right and can also be traded under the owner's willingness.
units.reusable_pattern: Hold a right and a market in the same sentence.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop either half.

units.rhetorical_move: adds a dynamic element
units.function: say what the new section introduces

original_instantiations: a dynamic element enters the model
it captures how value changes with time

units.source_excerpt: In this section we introduce a dynamic element to our model.
units.reusable_pattern: Open a section by naming the element it introduces.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not imply the element was always there.

units.rhetorical_move: simulates on a named graph model

original_instantiations: simulations run on an undirected scale-free graph
the graph model is chosen because it matches social networks

units.source_excerpt: We conduct simulations on an undirected scale-free graph generated by a named model.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the graph and the model that generates it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not substitute a different graph.

units.rhetorical_move: ties supervision to the buyer's value
units.function: give the rule as two cases

original_instantiations: high buyer value needs little supervision
low buyer value needs a set protection level

units.source_excerpt: If buyers value the information highly, the government need not supervise much.
units.reusable_pattern: State a policy as two cases split by one parameter.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a third case.

units.rhetorical_move: says quick reactions restore the equilibrium
units.function: name the response and its effect

original_instantiations: quick reactions bring the equilibrium back
awareness of protection is strengthened too

units.source_excerpt: By quick reactions, government can bring the equilibrium back to normal.
units.reusable_pattern: Credit a recovery to quick reactions.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not specify a speed the text does not.

units.rhetorical_move: splits what government can and cannot do

original_instantiations: government can do little about a negative externality
it can greatly improve welfare with a positive one

units.source_excerpt: Government can do little when disclosure has negative externality, but can greatly improve welfare otherwise.
units.reusable_pattern: Contrast what a government can do little about with what it can improve.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reverse the two cases.

units.rhetorical_move: extends the model to the network
units.function: say the base model is being extended

original_instantiations: the model is extended to the network effect
a named tax is then reconsidered

units.source_excerpt: We extend our model to take the network effect into consideration.
units.reusable_pattern: Announce an extension with we extend our model to.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat the extension as the base model.

units.rhetorical_move: explains the attachment rule

original_instantiations: a node attracts links in proportion to its degree
the rule is called a good approximation of social networks

units.source_excerpt: The probability of a new link is proportional to the node's degree.
units.reusable_pattern: State a network rule and call it an approximation.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call the approximation exact.

units.rhetorical_move: calls the model concise and powerful

original_instantiations: the sequential game is concise
it is also called powerful

units.source_excerpt: The sequential game is concise and powerful.
units.reusable_pattern: Praise a model with a pair of adjectives.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a third adjective.

units.rhetorical_move: calls one simulation quite new

original_instantiations: the network simulation is called quite new
the novelty is limited to related fields

units.source_excerpt: Simulating disclosure on a scale-free network is quite new in related fields.
units.reusable_pattern: Claim novelty with quite new and bound it to a field.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim novelty beyond the field.

units.rhetorical_move: says the implications are convincing and scientific

original_instantiations: the policy implications are direct and viable
they are also called convincing and scientific

units.source_excerpt: We give direct and viable policy implications, which are convincing and scientific.
units.reusable_pattern: Praise a result with two pairs of adjectives.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat the praise as evidence.

units.rhetorical_move: admits imperfect information is skipped

original_instantiations: imperfect information is not discussed
in reality the parameters are hard to obtain fully

units.source_excerpt: We do not discuss imperfect information, since the parameters are hard to obtain fully.
units.reusable_pattern: Admit an undiscussed case and say why reality makes it matter.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not discuss the case anyway.

units.rhetorical_move: blames a missing check on missing data

original_instantiations: robustness and sensitivity are not checked
the cause is a lack of data in reality

units.source_excerpt: We do not check the robustness due to the lack in data in reality.
units.reusable_pattern: Excuse a skipped check with due to the lack in data.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not invent the missing check.

units.rhetorical_move: calls the parameter forms subjective

original_instantiations: the parameter forms are subjective
only a rough quantitative form is given

units.source_excerpt: The forms of the parameters are subjective, and we only give a rough form.
units.reusable_pattern: Admit a form is subjective and call it rough.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the form as fitted.

units.rhetorical_move: limits the trade to one against one

original_instantiations: only one individual trades with one organization
many-to-one trades are left unexplored

units.source_excerpt: The model only considers a trade between one individual and one organization.
units.reusable_pattern: State the setting the model is limited to.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not apply the result beyond that setting.

units.rhetorical_move: blames an omission on time
units.function: give shortage of time as the cause

original_instantiations: one effect is not considered
the stated cause is a shortage of time

units.source_excerpt: We do not consider this effect due to a shortage of time.
units.reusable_pattern: Attribute an omission to a shortage of time.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not fill the omission in.

units.rhetorical_move: says selling brings benefits under conditions
units.function: restate the main result with its condition

original_instantiations: selling information brings benefits
only under certain circumstances, with government setting the price

units.source_excerpt: Under certain circumstances, selling information brings benefits to both sides.
units.reusable_pattern: Restate the result with its under certain circumstances condition.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the condition.

units.rhetorical_move: says older people grow unwilling

original_instantiations: older people are more unwilling to sell
the trend comes from differing risk attitudes

units.source_excerpt: As people grow older, they are more unwilling to sell their information.
units.reusable_pattern: State a trend with as people grow older.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reverse the direction.

units.rhetorical_move: hopes to dig deeper

original_instantiations: the topic will grow hotter
the authors hope to dig deeper if possible

units.source_excerpt: If possible, we hope that we could dig deeper into this field.
units.reusable_pattern: Close on if possible plus a hope to dig deeper.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not turn the hope into a plan.

units.rhetorical_move: admits the discussion is rough

original_instantiations: some discussions are rough and incomplete
the results still provide beneficial implications

units.source_excerpt: Though some discussions are rough and incomplete, the results provide beneficial implications.
units.reusable_pattern: Concede roughness with though, then claim the result still helps.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not delete the concession.

units.rhetorical_move: cites with bracketed journal tags

original_instantiations: each source ends with a bracketed journal tag
page ranges follow the year

units.source_excerpt: Sources close with a bracketed journal tag and a page range.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep the bracketed journal tag.
prohibited_generalizations: The citation format belongs to this list and does not transfer.

units.rhetorical_move: moves the derivations out of the body
units.function: point at the appendix for the algebra

original_instantiations: the algebra is placed in the appendix
the body keeps only the result

units.source_excerpt: The derivations are placed in the appendix rather than the body.
units.reusable_pattern: Defer the algebra to an appendix.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reproduce the algebra in the body.
